decision: Deep coordinates in plain scroll containers are owned by a new ledger entry P12 (paint, property trees, compositor, shaders: transforms become parent-relative exact offsets, folded to small window-relative f32 only at the GPU boundary), sequenced after L2. L2 owns the layout half as an interface constraint: child main-axis offsets are parent-relative and never rounded through absolute f32. ADR-0033 narrows its claim now: exact to 2^-20 px up to 2^43 px holds for scroll positions and virtual lists, plain-container content is placed and drawn exactly only below 2^22 device px until P12. SCROLL r15 only corrects the ADR text and adds one passing test pinning that bound, no rebasing in SCROLL. D001 was an accidental probe entry with no content and is void.
why: Codex r14 finding 2 reproduced: layout place.rs and compositor scroll.rs and compose.rs carry absolute window positions in f32 and the shader subtracts large f32s, so content past 2^23 px is not drawn and 1 px steps vanish at 36M px. The broken invariant is the ADR-0016 transform entry defined as an offset in window pixels, owned by the property trees, not by scroll motion. Fixing it inside SCROLL would rewrite layout place.rs concurrently with L2 and change ADR-0016, a standing decision that needs its own ADR. Virtual lists already rebase at the window origin (virtual_list.rs:954), so the millions-of-rows target is met today. Chrome caps near 33.5M px with LayoutUnit, an inherited limit we aim to beat, so plain containers are owned, not dropped.

decision: ADR-0035 D3 narrowed: in a check refuse only live Signal and Render-kind disposals; Scope/Effect/Computed disposal stays the arena's transaction; explicit Pipeline::close of a live window in a check now faults
why: Evidence: the cold check re-renders live instances and component::render retires their old render scopes via Scope::dispose on LIVE Scope nodes (arena-transactional, rolled back); refusing every live disposal faulted every check (engine::verify::a_check_cancelled_midway). Signals/trackers are disposed only by a value's end, the r19 I1 class. Architect to confirm or revise D3. | architect: Revised. Arena disposals are transactional because log_node keeps the live node whole (value Rc, closures, cleanups) and the check drops only clones, so a disposed live scope's Owned values and signals come back. But kind is the wrong discriminator: a misclassified Drop that calls Scope::dispose on a live scope would be rolled back with its only owner gone, the r19 I1 leak. Rule: refuse every live disposal entering Runtime::dispose in a check unless inside reactive::retiring closure, used only by engine re-run retirement (component::render old render scopes). before_rerun and cascades use dispose_index and are unaffected. No kind exemption. Pipeline::close of a live window in a check faults. Seeded mutant: plain Drop disposing a live root scope in a check faults. component.rs edit goes through the EM per D007. ADR-0035 D3 updated

decision: F1b r3 B: ADR-0035 D6 is narrowed (option ii). A write through interior mutability inside an app-chosen row/payload type (Collection snapshot rows are &T into an Arc tree shared with live; T: Cell<u8> is allowed) is T3, the same as any app heap. T1 keeps: the engine's own lent data (WorldRefCell, LogCell, chart pages, signal slots) cannot be written by a check through an engine lend; check admission is engine-only (round-3 A), so such a write needs an impure render/effect. Rejected: (i) a sealed no-interior-mutability bound (ForkData/Copy) on Collection rows breaks every app row type holding Rc/handles and is not expressible for 'no Cell' in stable Rust; (iii) copy-on-check costs O(rows) per check on million-row collections, breaking the M12 list budget, for a case only impure code reaches. Revisit if a pure (T2) path can write a row, or if the oracle finds a divergence from a row Cell.
why: Codex dff0fd38 repro collection_snapshot_lend opens a check from test code; once admission is engine-only (A), the only writer left is an impure render, which D6 already places in T3 for app heap. Option ii keeps the row type free and costs nothing on the hot path. | architect: Approved and generalised. The narrowing covers every store that lends an app-chosen T (Collection rows, signal and computed values, world-cell app payloads), not Collection alone. T1 covers engine-chosen data only. A pure OnceCell memo inside T stays T2. Consistent with ADR-0034 purity: a render writing a row Cell writes app heap other than through signals. Text in ADR-0035 D5 rule and D6.

decision: F1b r3 A: gui's raw check hooks (testing::check / in_check with a borrowing body) become #[cfg(test)] pub(crate), for gui's own tests only; gui's fork integration suites (fork_doom, fork_owns_only_its_own, fork_r17, fork_r18, fork_r19, fork_f1b2, fork_f1b3, teardown_cost, window_owns_work's one check test) move to crates/gui/tests/in_crate/ and compile into the gui lib test binary via #[cfg(test)] #[path] (with #[cfg(test)] extern crate self as gui). Other crates' per-thread-state tests (primitives tooltip/listbox/hover/select_lists, shadcn theme handle: 10 uses) keep one public debug-only doc(hidden) hook whose body must be 'static: gui::testing::in_check<R: 'static>(f: impl FnOnce() -> R + 'static). A 'static body cannot hold any lent borrow (&T, &mut T, a guard), so every round-2 repro (Debug, PartialEq, scoped thread, page formatter) is a compile error, by type, however user code is reached; the LENDS depth stays a debug backstop refusing a check inside a counted lend or render. Release builds have no hook at all (unchanged). Alternative rejected: converting the 10 cross-crate uses to a Scenario probe render (a GPU Scenario per unit test; a nested Scenario is equally reachable from a callback, so no stronger guarantee).
why: Round-3 brief A asks for admission no user code can reach with a lent borrow; the 'static bound gives that by construction for the one hook other crates need, and pub(crate) gives it for the rest. | architect: Approved with conditions. 1) The guarantee is the 'static body plus run-time refusal under a counted lend or a piece in use. Engine-only admission is not achievable by construction while Pipeline and Scenario are public, since a handler or Drop can drive a nested frame, and LENDS is what refuses it. So LENDS is a rule compiled wherever checks are (F2 release too), not a debug-only backstop. 2) LENDS stays per thread. Refusing checks off one UI thread is rejected because each test thread runs its own engine. 3) Simplest move: only bodies that must borrow go crate-internal. A 'static Result form may stay public beside in_check if that spares moving suites, and either way the round-2 repros stay as compile-fail doctests on the public hook plus in-crate refusal tests. 4) Downstream converts its 10 uses to move closures over cloned handles. No hot-path cost so performance-dx-lead sign-off is not required, inform them. ADR-0035 D4 round-3 text added.

decision: F1b r3 scoped_worker is not a T1 violation. A check owns what its body runs: foreign work a cooperative scheduler runs on a check's stack (rayon yield_local, a steal, a block_on of another executor) runs in that check's ambient world and is classed T3, the body's impurity. The repro's write is thread A's live code writing the payload A's own live lend handed it, on a borrow of A's world that no switch on B swaps, and rayon::scope runs the job with or without the check so live ends at 9 either way. T1's borrow bullet is sharpened to the switching thread's world. No code change for F1b beyond keeping the repro as a passing test that asserts 9 and documents the class. Process-wide LENDS, a !Send lend wrapper and a scheduler rule are rejected
why: The guarantee T1 gives is that live state after a check equals live state without it, and it holds here by counterfactual. Process-wide LENDS closes only this repro not the class (a job carrying an Arc or a mailbox Sender needs no lend) and makes parallel test threads refuse each other nondeterministically. A !Send wrapper cannot stop a reborrow of a Send payload. No toolkit can stop arbitrary cooperative executors from running foreign work on its stack. Engine checks open only on the UI thread whose one rayon use is install into gui's private layout pool from outside it, which blocks and never steals foreign jobs. Revisit if an engine check ever runs on a pool worker or an executor thread, or a Send engine handle writes live engine-chosen state without consulting the world it was made in
